research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Graduate student mothers navigate intertwined demands of graduate study and caregiving, yet little is known about how they seek support through online communities. We examine this through Mom Cafes, locally based online parenting communities in South. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: "Despite her age, Margaret was eager to make a change": Unpacking Aging Representations and Stereotypes in LLM-generated Stories
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate everyday stories, their portrayals can shape expectations about aging. Prior work has largely examined age stereotypes in short responses, leaving unanswered whose lives models default to imagining and how. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Bidirectional Modeling of mmWave Human Signals for Enhancement & Synthesis

research.title: DeepRadio: A Human-Agent Workspace for Physical Radio Development
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic programming can automate software-defined radio (SDR) development, but decisions can propagate from software to hardware without sufficient user visibility or control. We present DeepRadio, a human-agent workspace embedded in GNU Radio Companion (GRC) for jointly. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Driver Takeovers and Longitudinal Responses Analysis from Naturalistic Driving
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: As Level 2 advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) become more widely used, understanding driver-system interaction is increasingly important for traffic safety. However, limited real-world data make these interactions difficult to study. We present ADAS-TO, a naturalistic dataset. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Entering a New Domain in the Era of Generative AI: An Autoethnography of Solo Game Development as a Bioinformatics Educator
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid improvement of generative AI (GenAI) not only increased the efficiency of practice but also empowered individuals with capabilities to explore new domains. However, identity formation in the wake of such empowerment remains understudied. We. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: EventHOI: Event-Driven Resource-Efficient Hand-Object Interaction Logging on Smartglasses
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hand-object interactions (HOIs) can be captured by smartglasses to learn how people manipulate objects in daily life. Automatic logging of these interactions from an egocentric perspective provides time-stamped evidence of daily actions for applications like memory. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
